passage:
Coaching note: investor update rehearsal.

Pankaj ran his slides for me on Tuesday evening. Slide 3 said "traction remains strong." When I asked what it meant, he admitted that two of the three big clients had paused orders. His voice dropped when he said it. He'd been dreading the call all week, and it showed in how much he had polished the story.

I asked him what the investor, Uma, would rather hear: a smooth story now, or a difficult number early enough to help. Pankaj thought about it for a while.

He rewrote slide 3 with the paused orders, the reasons he knew, and two questions for Uma about who could introduce him to new buyers. He asked her what she would do, not only whether she would fund him.

He may lose some investors' patience. But Pankaj looked less afraid when he left. Follow-up next Tuesday.

qa.q: What did slide 3 of Pankaj's deck originally say?
qa.a: Slide 3 said that traction remains strong.

qa.q: Why did Pankaj polish the story so much, and what was he feeling?
qa.a: Pankaj dreaded the investor call all week, and polishing the story was a way of softening bad news he was afraid to deliver.

qa.q: What change to the slide helped, and why?
qa.a: Adding the paused orders and asking for introductions turned a surprise into an honest update and invited Uma's advice as well as money.

qa.q: How might Uma react to hearing the bad news early?
qa.a: Uma may be disappointed about the paused orders, but hearing it early and directly makes it easier to trust Pankaj and to help.

grounding: Dreading an investor update, Pankaj polishes the story too much; a coach's note shows him giving honest bad news early and asking for advice.
